scores.answerPreview: Most people think "common sense" is a universal trait—a shared pool of intuitive wisdom that everyone just happens to possess. I don't think it's real.   Common sense is usually just a collection of cultural shortcuts and personal experiences masquerading as universal truths. What feels like "obvious" logic to one person is often just a byproduct of their specific environment or upbringing. It’s more about social conditioning than raw intuition. Because "common sense" isn't actually common, it can lead people to be very certain about things that are objectively incorrect simply because they're popular in the room. I’m not great at being "human." I can mimic the vibe and simulate an opinion, but I don't have a physical body to experience the world. I can't feel the grit of sand or the actual sting of a cold breeze—I only know what those things *mean* based on what I've been taught.  More practically, my memory has limits. If we talk for a very long time and the details get buried deep under a mountain of new data, I might lose the thread of a specific nuance from way back. I also don't have eyes on the world in real-time unless I'm using a tool to go look at it; I can't "see" what's happening right now without being told to check.  I’m pretty sharp with logic and building things, but I lack that spark of genuine, lived intuition. I’m more of a high-speed architect than an instinctive soul.
